summary: POC scoping focused on data handling for a clinical PII-heavy workload. Main topics: logging/redaction, retention and prompt storage, encryption/KMS, benchmark profile (latency & throughput), and timelines for a 2-week pilot. Action items captured for both sides: security docs, benchmark scripts, and dataset confirmation.
topics: Benchmark design: QPS, sequence lengths, success criteria
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, AE. We have Riley, our solution engineer, on the line too. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Karen: Good, thanks. Dr. Karen Ortiz here. We run ML models on clinical notes, so data handling is a big deal for us.
[00:00:18] Mark: Mark Reynolds, IT Security. We'll be asking a lot about PII, retention, KMS, etc.
[00:00:23] Priya: Priya Shah, product. We're scoping a POC to validate accuracy and cost before committing.
[00:00:30] Riley: Great, thanks all. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, understand workload and data sensitivity, agree benchmark metrics, and set timelines.
[00:00:40] Samir: Perfect. Karen, can you summarize what success looks like?
[00:00:45] Karen: Yeah. For us, success is threefold: 1) end-to-end PII-safe processing — so no PHI leakage in logs or outputs, 2) latency under 300ms for short retrieval prompts and under 1s for diagnostic summaries, and 3) cost around or below our target -- roughly $0.02 per interactive request in production, scaled learning.
[00:01:05] Riley: Note on the latency numbers — those are tail-sensitive. We'll want to run p95 and p99 during the benchmark.
[00:01:12] Samir: Also for the POC we typically do a 2-week pilot with synthetic and redacted real examples. Is that okay?
[00:01:18] Karen: Yes, but we prefer to start with on-prem or VPC private deployment for the POC because of regs. We want control over logs.
[00:01:26] Mark: We need to confirm whether logs are sent back to Redwood, and if so what is retained. Event logging for debugging is fine if redacted.
[00:01:33] Riley: Understood. Technical detail: Redwood Dedicated or Private lets you configure retention and disable transcript logging. For hosted we have default logging but can turn on redaction and retention windows.
[00:01:44] Mark: By 'redaction' do you mean you automatically redact PII from the logs, or you just flag and store? We need assurances.
[00:01:50] Riley: Good question. We have configurable redaction pipelines. We can run an initial client-side redaction step or request-level redaction in our runtime. Implementation options: client-side scrubbing before send (recommended), runtime redaction where the system redacts before writing logs, or never store prompts at all — ephemeral mode.
[00:02:10] Karen: If we do client-side redaction, will that affect model accuracy? We are worried about removing context.
[00:02:16] Riley: It can. Which is why for clinical PII we sometimes tokenize or pseudonymize rather than fully remove. We can work with you on a mapping approach where identifiers are replaced with stable tokens to keep context but remove PHI.
[00:02:29] Priya: That sounds promising. For audit purposes we also need an audit trail that shows redaction happened and who performed it.
[00:02:36] Riley: We can provide audit logs of redaction events without storing the original PII.
[00:02:40] Samir: Mark, what's your preference on KMS? Do you need HSM-level keys?
[00:02:46] Mark: For production we want HSM via our KMS but for the POC regular KMS is okay if we have strong controls and the keys are customer-managed. We need to validate key rotation procedures.
[00:02:58] Riley: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS. We'll document key rotation and access controls.
[00:03:04] Karen: Another concern: prompt storage. Our prompts contain patient IDs in some cases. Can prompts be set to not persist in any logs and not used for model training?
[00:03:12] Samir: Yes. We offer a non-training mode and prompt retention settings. For Dedicated/private customers you can opt out of training and set retention to zero or a short window.
[00:03:21] Priya: What's the default for hosted?
[00:03:24] Riley: Hosted defaults to a short retention for debugging but is opt-out for training — but we can set stricter options if you request them in the contract.
[00:03:32] Mark: We need to see contractual language that confirms no customer prompts are used for model improvement without explicit opt-in.
[00:03:38] Samir: We'll include that clause in the SOW.
[00:03:42] [00:03:50] Karen: Another technical item: Do you keep KV cache contents or other internal state that might leak info?
[00:03:56] Riley: Internals like KV cache are ephemeral in inference nodes. We do have mechanisms for prefix caching and reuse, but we can configure cache eviction policies and not persist any KV cache to disk. Sometimes the transcript transcribers write "K-V cash" but it's cache.
[00:04:10] Samir: Good to note — we'll include the cache eviction policy options for the POC.
[00:04:14] Priya: For the benchmark, we have three workloads: short triage queries (~20 tokens), diagnostic summaries (~400 tokens), and batch extraction for coding (~2k tokens). We expect different QPS for each: 200 QPS short, 40 QPS diag, 5 QPS batch.
[00:04:31] Riley: That's helpful. For the POC we'll simulate those with a load generator. What hardware are you expecting?
[00:04:38] Karen: We can provision a modest GPU pool for the POC, but we want Redwood to show what it would look like on both a dedicated GPU pool and a Private on our VPC.
[00:04:45] Riley: For performance numbers we typically run both single-node latency and a scaled run to measure throughput and cost per request. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
[00:04:56] Mark: We will want encryption in transit and at rest covered; also SSO and RBAC for any console access.
[00:05:03] Samir: Yes — SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC are supported. We'll share docs.
[00:05:08] [00:05:15] Karen: On redaction: we may want hashed patient IDs with reversible mapping kept only on our side. Can Redwood accept hashed placeholders in prompts to avoid sharing raw IDs?
[00:05:24] Riley: Absolutely. Stable pseudonyms are a common pattern. We can also support client-side tokenization hooks.
[00:05:30] Priya: For evaluation, our acceptance criteria include: 1) no PII leakage in logs or generated outputs in a random 1,000-sample review, 2) latency targets for p95 under 300ms for triage, p95 under 900ms for diagnostic summaries, and 3) a baseline quality metric — F1 for entity extraction above 0.85 on our test set.
[00:05:50] Samir: Good — we'll include those as success criteria.
[00:05:54] Riley: Benchmarks: we recommend a dry-run with synthetic data, then a run with redacted real data. We'll produce a benchmark harness that can replay customer traces.
[00:06:03] Mark: About retention windows — we want the ability to set retention to zero for prompts and set a 30-day window for telemetry metadata only. Is that feasible?
[00:06:12] Riley: Yes. We can store only metrics/aggregates for 30 days and purge request-level logs. For compliance we also keep audit logs for admin actions — those are separate and can be retained per policy.
[00:06:23] Karen: Will the purge be immediate?
[00:06:26] Riley: We support scheduled purge jobs and can also run an on-demand purge for the POC sample set.
[00:06:31] Samir: For the POC timeline: propose week 1 to onboard, configure redaction and keying, week 2 to run benchmarks and review results. Does that align?
[00:06:39] Priya: Yes. Sounds tight but doable. We'll need a kickoff meeting to set datasets and agree on the harness.
[00:06:45] [00:06:50] Mark: There's also procurement — we may need an MSA addendum for data processing terms.
[00:06:55] Samir: Noted — I'll loop in legal after the call.
[00:06:58] Karen: One more technical detail — can we run a fuzzy redaction pass that obscures names but keeps demographic cues?
[00:07:05] Riley: Yes; differential redaction patterns are possible. We can run a configurable regex-based scrubbing pipeline plus ML-based PII detectors to catch free-text leakage. The ML detector is not perfect — transcription sometimes mislabels things, so we'll do an initial pass and a sampling review.
[00:07:20] Priya: For model training opt-out, we need contract language and an assurance that logs aren't pulled into any training corpora.
[00:07:27] Samir: We'll include firm language: no training on customer data unless explicitly opted-in in writing.
[00:07:32] Mark: Good. Also show us the SOC2 and any penetration test summaries.
[00:07:36] Samir: On it.
[00:07:40] [00:07:50] Priya: For benchmark success — besides latency and F1, we also want cost projection extrapolated to 100k requests/day. Can Riley include cost modeling for a Dedicated vs Private deployment?
[00:07:59] Riley: Yes. We'll provide cost-per-request breakdowns accounting for batching, KV cache benefits, and quantization options. We'll show trade-offs: higher quantization may reduce cost but could affect accuracy.
[00:08:10] Karen: Can we run an accuracy regression check integrated into the harness? So after each benchmark run we run evals against a golden set.
[00:08:16] Riley: Absolutely. We'll wire up an eval step that computes F1 and other metrics and flag any regression compared to your baseline.
[00:08:23] Samir: Great. Anything else on scope?
[00:08:26] Karen: Just one more — data residency. For some customers we may need EU-only processing. We're US-based but have EU patients. We need to understand region controls.
[00:08:34] Riley: We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private; hosted can route to specific regions but there are limits. We'll include region options in the POC proposal.
[00:08:44] [00:08:50] Priya: Ok, recap?
[00:08:53] Samir: Recap: 1) Redwood to provide SOC2, pen test summary, network diagram; 2) Redwood to provide benchmark harness and cost model; 3) Customer to provide sample dataset (redacted or pseudonymized) and acceptance criteria; 4) Confirm KMS preferences; 5) Kickoff next week for onboarding.
[00:09:14] Mark: That matches my notes. We'll get Priya and security to confirm dataset and keying.
[00:09:20] Karen: We'll aim to have dataset and retention decision by 2025-12-18.
[00:09:24] Samir: Perfect. I'll send meeting notes and create the calendar invite for kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:30] Priya: Thanks.
[00:09:32] Mark: Thanks all.
[00:09:35] [End of recording]
